meta.note_to_dev: Structured fields (interest, difficulty, structure, free, grade, deadline, time_commitment) are authoritative here and drive the quiz/nav. Detail prose (what_it_is, what_you_need_to_do, full_timeline, notes) merged from competitions_full.csv. Owner updates this file weekly. Null deadline = date TBD: sort last, never show negative/NaN countdown.

field_definitions.difficulty: Beginner = low barrier, solo-possible, short time commitment, good first competition. Intermediate = requires real prep or a team. Advanced = serious multi-month effort or selective. Elite = nationally prestigious, highly selective, resume-defining.
field_definitions.why_it_helps: One sentence on the application value. Written for a student, not a judge.
field_definitions.teacher_required: true if a teacher/advisor/coach must register or sponsor the student
field_definitions.free: true if free to enter (ignore optional finalist/travel costs; note those in cost_note)

competitions.name: Marshall Society Essay Competition (Cambridge)
competitions.deadline_display: Submissions due August 30, 2026, 11:59 PM UK time
competitions.why_it_helps: A short economics essay judged by Cambridge students, a fast, solo way to show academic writing ability on a college app without a team or teacher.
competitions.what_it_is: An international economics essay contest run by the Marshall Society, the undergraduate economics society at the University of Cambridge.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Pick one of the annual prompts and write an analytical essay under 1,250 words focused on logical reasoning, strong evidence, and original economic argument. Submit as a PDF.
competitions.full_timeline: Prompts released July 2026. Submissions due August 30, 2026.
competitions.notes: Closes in days. If nobody enters this year, it returns next July.

competitions.name: Young Investors Society (YIS) Global Stock Pitch
competitions.deadline_note: Report + video historically due ~Feb 20; registration opens Oct 15, 2026
competitions.deadline_display: Pitch report and video historically due February 20, 11:59 PM PST
competitions.why_it_helps: You do real equity research and pitch a stock to professional investors, a standout, under-the-radar credential for anyone eyeing finance or business.
competitions.what_it_is: A global stock pitching competition where students act as analysts, running fundamental analysis on a public company and pitching it to professional investors.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Pick a publicly traded company, perform financial analysis and valuation, write a full equity research report, and record a video pitch arguing buy or sell.
competitions.full_timeline: Registration opens October 15, 2026. Report and video deadline historically February 20. State and regional rounds lead to global finals.
competitions.notes: No advisor needed. One of the few finance competitions a student can enter alone.

competitions.name: Wharton Global High School Investment Competition
competitions.deadline_note: Team account due Sep 11, 2026 (5pm ET); registration opens Aug 10
competitions.why_it_helps: A Wharton-run team competition managing a virtual $100k portfolio, name-brand prestige and a real deliverable (a strategy paper) you can talk about in interviews.
competitions.what_it_is: An online investment competition run by Wharton where high school teams manage a $100,000 virtual portfolio and build a strategic plan for a specific client.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Form a team, analyze company financial reports, execute trades in Wharton's simulator, and write both a mid-project strategy report and a final portfolio strategy paper covering asset allocation and investment thesis.
competitions.full_timeline: Registration opened August 10, closes September 11, 2026. Team account with advisor required by then.
competitions.notes: BLOCKER: an adult advisor must be attached to the team account before the deadline.

competitions.name: High School Fed Challenge
competitions.deadline_note: Registration closes Feb 15, 2027; final paper due Mar 15
competitions.deadline_display: Registration closes February 15. Final paper due March 15, 2027.
competitions.why_it_helps: You analyze real macro data and defend a monetary-policy call to actual Federal Reserve economists, top teams get published, a genuinely elite econ credential.
competitions.what_it_is: A Federal Reserve competition where students analyze economic data, evaluate macroeconomic conditions, and recommend monetary policy. Winners are recognized by the Fed and published in the Journal of Future Economists.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Research macro trends, inflation, employment, and banking conditions. Produce a formal economic podcast script or academic paper depending on your regional Fed district's format. Present your policy recommendation and defend it in Q&A with Fed economists.
competitions.full_timeline: Registration opens September 10, 2026 and closes February 15, 2027. Final research paper due March 15, 2027.
competitions.notes: Run nationwide by the Federal Reserve System, not district by district. Up to 3 research assistants beyond the 3-5 presenters. Format is a podcast script or academic paper.

competitions.name: National Economics Challenge (CEE)
competitions.deadline_note: Teacher registration Jan 1-early Apr 2027; state exams late Feb-late Mar
competitions.deadline_display: State prelim exams late February to late March 2027
competitions.why_it_helps: The flagship national econ team competition, a clear signal of economics depth with divisions for both beginners and advanced students.
competitions.what_it_is: The flagship national high school economics competition, run by the Council for Economic Education, testing microeconomics, macroeconomics, and current international events.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Your coach registers the team, receives test credentials, and proctors the online exams through CEE's EconChallenge portal. Compete in either the David Ricardo division (first-time econ students) or the Adam Smith division (AP, IB, or advanced).
competitions.full_timeline: Teacher registration opens January 1, 2027 and closes around early April 2027. Most states run online prelims late February to late March. Top teams advance to national semifinals and a live Quiz Bowl final.
competitions.notes: BLOCKER: coach must register and proctor. Division choice matters, Adam Smith is significantly harder.

competitions.name: Harvard International Economics Essay Contest
competitions.cost_detail: $20 reading fee for US students, $30 international.
competitions.deadline_note: Historically due ~Jan 5; prompts released late Oct
competitions.why_it_helps: A Harvard-affiliated economics essay contest, a solo writing credential with a recognizable name attached.
competitions.what_it_is: An international essay competition run by the Harvard Undergraduate Economics Association with the Harvard International Review.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Pick one of four released prompts and write an analytical essay under a strict 1,500-word limit. Cite everything in APA or Chicago. Submit as a PDF before the deadline.
competitions.full_timeline: Prompts historically released late October. Submissions typically due January 5.
competitions.notes: One of the few paid entries in this section. Word limit is enforced strictly.

competitions.name: John Locke Essay Competition
competitions.why_it_helps: Oxford/Princeton-judged essays across seven disciplines, prestigious, intellectually serious, and a strong signal for humanities and social-science applicants.
competitions.what_it_is: An international essay competition run by the John Locke Institute, judged by scholars from Oxford and Princeton, covering Philosophy, Politics, Economics, History, Psychology, Theology, and Law.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Choose one official prompt and write a persuasive essay up to 2,000 words. Build a strong thesis backed by theory, logic, and empirical evidence.
competitions.full_timeline: Prompts released early February 2027. Submission deadline May 31, 2027.
competitions.notes: Must be 18 or younger on the submission deadline. Registration deadline is separate from and earlier than submission. Late entries have historically carried a fee.

competitions.name: National Personal Finance Challenge (CEE)
competitions.deadline_display: WA registration window early January to mid-April 2027
competitions.why_it_helps: A team competition on real personal-finance decision-making, practical and approachable, good for students newer to economics.
competitions.what_it_is: A CEE national competition testing personal finance, financial planning, and money management.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Compete in state testing covering earning income, spending, saving, investing, managing credit, and managing risk. Top state teams build and present a financial plan for a fictitious family to expert judges.
competitions.full_timeline: WA team registration early January to mid-April 2027. Online preliminary exam window falls in the same range. Top state teams advance to National Finals.
competitions.notes: Same organizer as NEC. One teacher can plausibly run both.

competitions.name: Berkeley Economic Review Essay Contest
competitions.why_it_helps: A short econ essay for a UC Berkeley peer-reviewed journal, low barrier, solo, and a real publication-adjacent credential.
competitions.what_it_is: An international essay contest hosted by UC Berkeley's undergraduate peer-reviewed economics journal.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Write an original essay under 1,000 words responding to the semester's featured prompt. Support the argument with credible academic sources and submit through their portal.
competitions.full_timeline: Prompts expected early February 2027. Submission deadline typically mid-March 2027.
competitions.notes: 1,000 words is short. Free, individual, no advisor. Low cost of entry relative to signal.

competitions.name: International Economics Olympiad
competitions.cost_note: Free if selected for national team
competitions.cost_detail: Free to participate if selected for the national team.
competitions.why_it_helps: The international econ olympiad, an elite, globally recognized signal for the most serious economics students.
competitions.what_it_is: An annual international competition testing Economics, Financial Literacy, and Business.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Qualify through the national pipeline. At the international event you complete three stages: a written exam on general economics, a financial literacy game simulation, and a 24-hour team business case study presented to international judges.
competitions.full_timeline: Registration closes February 27, 2027. Round 1 exam, open to all, March 13, 2027 at 5:00 PM PST. Qualifiers move through the national pipeline to the international event.
competitions.notes: Round 1 uses remote anti-cheating proctoring. Under 20 and not enrolled in university.

competitions.name: DECA
competitions.cost_detail: National dues $8 plus state and local dues, typically $20 to $40 total. Conference registration $50 to $150+ per level.
competitions.why_it_helps: A huge business org with roleplay and case events, an accessible on-ramp to business competition that colleges recognize instantly.
competitions.what_it_is: One of the largest international business student organizations, preparing students for careers in marketing, finance, hospitality, and management through case studies, roleplays, and written business plans.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Join your school's chapter, pick a competitive event such as an individual roleplay or team decision-making, and take a 100-question career cluster exam proctored by your advisor.
competitions.full_timeline: Districts November 2026 to January 2027. State conferences February and March 2027. ICDC April 2027.
competitions.notes: Requires an active school chapter. Highest recurring cost on this list once conference fees stack.

competitions.name: FBLA
competitions.cost_detail: National dues $10 plus state and local, typically $15 to $30 total. Conference fees apply for state and national.
competitions.deadline_display: Regional and state qualifiers January to April 2027
competitions.why_it_helps: 70+ business events including cybersecurity and public speaking, and you can join as a virtual member if your school has no chapter, low barrier, broad appeal.
competitions.what_it_is: Future Business Leaders of America, with over 70 competitive events across accounting, finance, cybersecurity, public speaking, and entrepreneurship.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Compete in objective tests or presentation events at regional and state conferences. If your school has no chapter you can either charter one with a faculty advisor and a few classmates, or join as a virtual or direct independent member and still compete at state and national.
competitions.full_timeline: Regionals and state January to April 2027. National Leadership Conference late June 2027.
competitions.notes: The virtual membership path is the workaround if no chapter exists. Worth flagging prominently, most students do not know it exists.

competitions.name: Blue Ocean Competition
competitions.why_it_helps: The largest virtual entrepreneurship pitch competition, no teacher needed, all you need is an idea and a video pitch, a clean solo/team entrepreneurship credential.
competitions.what_it_is: The largest virtual high school entrepreneurship competition in the world. Students pitch original business concepts that create new market space rather than competing in existing markets.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Develop a business idea using Blue Ocean strategy, build a slide deck, and record a 3 to 5 minute video pitch covering value proposition and market strategy. Submit online for review by entrepreneurs and business leaders.
competitions.full_timeline: Registration opened May 13, 2026. Pitch submissions due February 21, 2027.
competitions.notes: Start early. Customer validation and iteration are what separate placing entries from the rest.

competitions.name: Diamond Challenge
competitions.why_it_helps: A University of Delaware global startup competition with real pitch rounds, a serious entrepreneurship signal with a summit finalists attend.
competitions.what_it_is: A global entrepreneurship competition from Horn Entrepreneurship at the University of Delaware, focused on creative problem-solving and startup building.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Develop a startup concept in either the Business Innovation or Social Innovation track. Submit a pitch deck of up to 15 slides and a 3-minute video pitch.
competitions.full_timeline: Submissions open September 2026, due mid-January 2027. Semifinalists advance to virtual or live regional pitch rounds. Summit April 2027.
competitions.notes: Any adult can serve as advisor, not necessarily a teacher. Ages 14-18.

competitions.name: Conrad Challenge
competitions.cost_detail: Free to submit. $499 for the Innovation Stage. $499 per guest for the Summit.
competitions.why_it_helps: STEM-meets-business innovation solving global challenges, blends entrepreneurship with technical work, strong for students at that intersection.
competitions.what_it_is: A global innovation competition where teams use STEM, business design, and entrepreneurship to build commercially viable solutions to major global challenges.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Pick a category such as Aerospace, Cyber-Technology, Health, or Sustainability. Complete Phase 1 (Investor Pitch), then Phase 2 (Business Plan, Innovation Brief, and Video). Finalists present live at the Summit.
competitions.full_timeline: Registration opens August 27, 2026 and closes October 29, 2026. Innovation Stage runs from October 29, 2026 to early January 2027. Finalists present at the Conrad Innovation Summit.
competitions.notes: The $499 Innovation Stage fee is the highest barrier in this section and it hits AFTER you submit Phase 1. Say so up front. Source doc had a 2027 typo in the Innovation Stage start year.

competitions.name: NFTE World Series of Innovation
competitions.why_it_helps: Corporate-sponsored innovation challenges tied to UN goals, low barrier, no teacher required, a good first entrepreneurship entry.
competitions.what_it_is: An international entrepreneurship competition from the Network for Teaching Entrepreneurship, built around business solutions aligned to the UN Sustainable Development Goals.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Pick one of several corporate-sponsored challenge categories. Create a product or service concept, build a business proposal covering target market and revenue model, and submit online.
competitions.full_timeline: Challenges launch September 9, 2026 at 6:00 AM PST. Submissions due December 13, 2026.
competitions.notes: Ages 13-19, grades 7-12. No advisor required.

competitions.name: Technovation Girls
competitions.deadline_note: Registration opens Oct 2026; submissions late Apr 2027
competitions.why_it_helps: Young women build a real app or AI prototype plus a business plan, combines tech and entrepreneurship into one standout project.
competitions.what_it_is: A global technology entrepreneurship program where young women code mobile apps or AI tools to solve real community problems.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Identify a community issue, code a mobile app or design an AI prototype, write a full business plan, and produce a 2-minute pitch video.
competitions.full_timeline: Registration opens October 2026. Season runs January to April 2027. Submissions due late April 2027.
competitions.notes: ELIGIBILITY: girls only, Senior Division ages 15-18. Requires an adult mentor. Cross-listed under Math & Computer Science.

competitions.name: Paradigm Challenge
competitions.why_it_helps: Solve a global problem in any medium (invention, app, video, program), flexible and open-ended, a friendly first competition.
competitions.what_it_is: An international competition from Project Paradigm where youth use STEM, business design, media, or civic engagement to solve global issues in health, safety, or environmental waste.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Build a solution to the current challenge topic in any medium: an invention, business proposal, app, video, or community program. Submit a written summary and supporting materials on impact and implementation.
competitions.full_timeline: Two-year cycle. Entries opened May 2, 2025 and close May 1, 2027.
competitions.notes: Runs on a two-year cycle, so the window is long and the format is very open. Both cut two ways: no time pressure means no forcing function.

competitions.name: Wharton Global High School Data Science Competition
competitions.why_it_helps: Wharton-run sports analytics using real datasets, bridges business and data science with a name-brand host.
competitions.what_it_is: A global sports analytics and data science competition from the Wharton Sports Analytics and Business Initiative and Wharton Global Youth.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Use provided real-world sports datasets to build statistical models, analyze player and team performance, predict outcomes, and submit a technical report on your insights and methodology.
competitions.full_timeline: Registration opens January 2027. Datasets released February 2027. Submissions due March 2027. Virtual finals April 2027.
competitions.notes: Same organizer as the Wharton Investment Competition. Ages 14-18.

competitions.name: MIT THINK Scholars
competitions.why_it_helps: Uniquely rewards a strong research proposal rather than finished work, MIT mentorship and funding, ideal if you have an idea but lack lab resources.
competitions.what_it_is: Rather than judging finished research, THINK funds students who have done deep background work on a project but lack the resources to build it. Selected students get mentorship and a budget.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Write a project proposal in science, tech, or engineering. Strong proposals have an insightful idea, clearly defined goals, and a realistic implementation procedure. Start well before November.
competitions.full_timeline: Applications open Nov 1, 2026. Due Jan 1, 2027. Winners receive funding and MIT mentorship.
competitions.notes: US residents only.

competitions.name: Science Fair Pathway (CSRSEF → WSSEF → ISEF)
competitions.cost_detail: [Central Sound Regional Science & Engineering Fair] Free to enter. [Washington State Science & Engineering Fair] $30 per student. [Regeneron ISEF] Free for finalists.
competitions.deadline_note: Central Sound Regional Mar 6, 2027; WSSEF Apr 2-3; ISEF May 8-14
competitions.why_it_helps: The premier research pathway in high school science, advancing toward ISEF is one of the strongest STEM credentials a student can earn.
competitions.what_it_is: [Central Sound Regional Science & Engineering Fair] The ISEF-affiliated regional fair for the Central Sound area. You present to local industry professionals and academics, get feedback, and compete for advancement. [Washington State Science & Engineering Fair] The state fair. High schoolers from across Washington present independent research and compete within a single category. [Regeneron ISEF] The world's largest and most prestigious pre-college STEM competition. Roughly 1,800 finalists from more than 60 countries compete for nearly $9 million in prizes and scholarships.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: [Central Sound Regional Science & Engineering Fair] Run an original science or engineering project inside a continuous 12-month window. Secure ISEF approval BEFORE testing if it involves human participants, vertebrate animals, hazardous biological agents, or hazardous chemicals. Submit Forms 1, 1A, 1B and a research plan. Keep a daily digital logbook. [Washington State Science & Engineering Fair] You do not need to win at CSRSEF to attend, but King and Snohomish county students must participate in their regional fair first. A high placement in your category does not guarantee ISEF. Only Grand Champion awards advance. [Regeneron ISEF] You cannot enter directly. Qualify through the regional and state fair pipeline. Note the booth rules: no live organisms, no unshielded high voltage, no liquids including water, no hazardous chemicals active at the exhibition booth.
competitions.full_timeline: [Central Sound Regional Science & Engineering Fair] Fair March 6, 2027 at Mountlake Terrace High School. Top projects advance to WSSEF. Grand Champion advances directly to ISEF. [Washington State Science & Engineering Fair] April 2-3, 2027. High school competes April 3. Grand Champions (roughly top 9-10 projects) form the WISE team that goes to ISEF. [Regeneron ISEF] May 8-14, 2027. Entry is by qualification through WSSEF Grand Champion only.
competitions.notes: [Central Sound Regional Science & Engineering Fair] Advisor must be on record BEFORE registration. Cannot have reached age 20 before May 1 of competition year. King/Snohomish students must do this fair before WSSEF. [Washington State Science & Engineering Fair] Cannot have reached age 20 before May 1 of competition year. [Regeneron ISEF] Qualification required. Start at CSRSEF.

competitions.name: Davidson Fellows Scholarship
competitions.why_it_helps: Up to $50k for a significant, near-peer-reviewed body of work, an elite scholarship that signals genuine original contribution to a field.
competitions.what_it_is: One of the most demanding scholarships available. Awards $50,000, $25,000, or $10,000 to students 18 and under for a significant completed body of work in STEM, literature, music, philosophy, or an outside-the-box category.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Submit a completed, original work that makes a genuine contribution to your field. For STEM that usually means research that could be peer-reviewed or already is. Also required: a written overview, a video presentation, and letters of recommendation. Successful applicants often spend 12 to 24 months on the work.
competitions.full_timeline: 2027 application opens Fall 2026. Typical deadline mid-February.
competitions.notes: Must be 18 or younger. Exact 2027 date not confirmed.

competitions.name: Breakthrough Junior Challenge
competitions.why_it_helps: Explain a science concept in a 2-minute video, no lab or team needed, the most accessible way into prestigious STEM competition and a huge scholarship upside.
competitions.what_it_is: A global science video competition. Students explain one big idea in physics, mathematics, or the life sciences in under two minutes. The overall winner receives a $250,000 college scholarship, money for their teacher, and a new science lab for their school.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Make an original video of two minutes or less explaining a scientific concept. Animated, live-action, or both. Then score at least five other students' videos in the peer review round, which is required to complete your entry. Regional champions are decided partly by likes and positive reactions across Breakthrough's social channels.
competitions.full_timeline: Opens May, closes mid-September annually. Peer review follows submission.
competitions.notes: Ages 13-18. Popularity voting is part of judging, so plan distribution, not just the video.

competitions.name: GENIUS Olympiad
competitions.cost_detail: $50 application fee per project. $500 participant registration if selected as a finalist.
competitions.why_it_helps: Environmental projects across science, writing, business, art, and film, flexible entry points make it approachable across disciplines.
competitions.what_it_is: An international project competition focused entirely on environmental issues, across Science, Writing, Business, Robotics, Art, Music, and Short Film.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Build and submit a project addressing an environmental problem. Depending on category this ranges from lab research on renewable energy to an artwork or a sustainability business plan. Submit online for initial judging to earn a finals invitation.
competitions.full_timeline: Applications due March 7, 2027. Finalists announced March 25, 2027. Global finals June 8-11, 2027 in Rochester, NY.
competitions.notes: Ages 13-18. The $500 finalist fee plus travel to Rochester is the real cost. Budget before entering.

competitions.name: Research Publication (NHSJS, JEI)
competitions.cost_note: Free to submit; publishing fee possible
competitions.cost_detail: Free to submit, publishing fee may apply.
competitions.why_it_helps: Getting original research formally published is a rare, concrete credential, rolling deadlines mean you can submit whenever your paper is ready.
competitions.what_it_is: Peer-reviewed journals that publish original research by high schoolers. NHSJS and JEI are the two most established.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Write a full formal manuscript with Abstract, Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References. Submit through the journal portal with mentor or teacher consent forms. Expect peer review and required revisions before publication.
competitions.full_timeline: Rolling submissions. Review and revision often takes several months, so submit as soon as the paper is done.
competitions.notes: NHSJS grades 9-12, JEI grades 6-12. Requires a professor or senior mentor. Second URL: emerginginvestigators.org

competitions.name: US Physics Olympiad (USAPhO)
competitions.cost_detail: $35 to $50 school site registration plus $3 to $6 per student for the F=ma exam.
competitions.deadline_note: F=ma exam Feb 12, 2027; registration opens mid-late Sep
competitions.deadline_display: Registration closes mid-to-late January 2027. Exam February 12, 2027.
competitions.why_it_helps: The main path to the US Physics Team, high placement is a top-tier signal for physics and engineering applicants.
competitions.what_it_is: The premier US high school physics competition, run by AAPT. It is the primary path onto the U.S. Physics Team.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Take the F=ma exam, a 75-minute multiple choice test on algebra-based classical mechanics. High scorers advance to USAPhO, a calculus-based free-response exam covering mechanics, E&M, thermodynamics, and optics.
competitions.full_timeline: Registration opens mid-to-late September 2026, closes mid-to-late January 2027. F=ma exam expected February 12, 2027. High scorers advance to USAPhO.
competitions.notes: BLOCKER: a teacher must register the school as an official testing site through the AAPT portal. Ask the physics teacher, department head, or counselor.

competitions.name: US Chemistry Olympiad (USNCO)
competitions.cost_detail: Free for most local ACS sections.
competitions.why_it_helps: The national chemistry olympiad, advancing signals serious chemistry ability, and the local exam is right here at Bellevue College.
competitions.what_it_is: A multi-tier chemistry competition run by the American Chemical Society to identify top high school chemistry students nationally.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Sign up through your school or the local ACS section for the Local Chemistry Olympiad Exam. Check the school Chemistry Club. Top performers advance to the National Exam: multiple choice, written free response, and a hands-on lab practical.
competitions.full_timeline: WA Puget Sound section usually hosts the local exam at Bellevue College in March. National Exam set by ACS for mid-April 2027.
competitions.notes: Students under 20. Exact local exam date not confirmed.

competitions.name: USA Biology Olympiad (USABO)
competitions.cost_detail: $125 school registration fee covering all students.
competitions.deadline_note: Open Exam Feb 2027; school registration opens late fall 2026
competitions.deadline_display: School registration opens late fall 2026. Open Exam February 2027.
competitions.why_it_helps: The premier biology olympiad, a strong credential for pre-med and life-science applicants.
competitions.what_it_is: The premier US high school biology competition, sponsored by the Center for Excellence in Education. It selects the U.S. team for the International Biology Olympiad.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Register through your school for the Open Exam, a 50-minute multiple choice test covering cellular biology, plant anatomy, genetics, ecology, and ethology.
competitions.full_timeline: School registration late fall 2026. Open Exam February 2027. Top 10% advance to Semifinals. Top 20 attend a two-week national training camp.
competitions.notes: BLOCKER: school must register. One $125 fee covers every student, so recruiting classmates lowers nobody's cost but makes the ask easier on the teacher.

competitions.name: Science Olympiad
competitions.deadline_display: Registration opens early fall 2026. Tournaments January to April 2027.
competitions.why_it_helps: 23 events across every science discipline in a team format, something for everyone and a well-known team credential.
competitions.what_it_is: The largest team-based STEM competition in the US, with 23 events spanning biology, chemistry, physics, earth science, and engineering design.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Join or form a 15-student school team. Pair up with teammates to study, run labs, or build devices like bridges, gliders, and towers, then compete against other schools.
competitions.full_timeline: Team registration typically opens early fall. Invitational, regional, state, and national tournaments run January through April 2027.
competitions.notes: Division C is grades 9-12, maximum seven 12th graders on a 15-student team. Needs 15 committed students and a school advisor, the highest coordination cost on this list.

competitions.name: AMC 10/12 → AIME → USAMO Pathway
competitions.cost_detail: School registration $50 to $100, plus $25 to $30 per bundle of 10 booklets. Often covered by the school or charged as a $10 to $15 student fee.
competitions.why_it_helps: The foundational US math pipeline; qualifying for AIME and USAMO is one of the most recognized elite signals on any STEM application.
competitions.what_it_is: The premier US high school mathematics pipeline, run by the Mathematical Association of America. AMC 10/12 leads to AIME, which leads to the national olympiads.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Register through your school or an approved testing center. Take a 25-question, 75-minute multiple choice exam with no calculator. High scorers earn an AIME invitation, which is the qualifier for the US national olympiad teams.
competitions.full_timeline: Registration opens late summer 2026. AMC 10/12 November 2026. AIME February 2027. USAMO and USAJMO follow for qualifiers.
competitions.notes: BLOCKER, HIGHEST PRIORITY: your school must register as an official MAA testing site, and that window closes well before the November exam. AMC 10 is grades 10 and below, under 17.5 years. AMC 12 is grades 12 and below, under 19.5 years.

competitions.name: USACO
competitions.why_it_helps: A self-serve competitive programming ladder, no teacher needed, and division promotions (Silver/Gold/Platinum) are a clear CS signal.
competitions.what_it_is: The USA Computing Olympiad, a four-division competitive programming ladder leading to the US team for the International Olympiad in Informatics.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Create a free account and enter a contest weekend. Everyone starts at Bronze. You get 4 hours in a self-scheduled window to solve 3 algorithmic problems in C++, Java, or Python. A high score promotes you to Silver, then Gold, then Platinum.
competitions.full_timeline: Four online contests per season, running monthly from December 2026 through the US Open in March 2027.
competitions.notes: LOWEST BARRIER ON THE ENTIRE HUB. No teacher, no team, no fee, no permission. A student can register tonight. Feature this one.

competitions.name: Congressional App Challenge
competitions.why_it_helps: Build any app on any topic and get recognized by your member of Congress, low barrier, high recognition, a great first CS project.
competitions.what_it_is: A nationwide coding competition hosted by Members of Congress. Each district judges its own entries, so the applicant pool you compete against is small.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Design and code an original app, mobile, web, desktop, or tablet, in any language on any topic. Submit a 3-minute video explaining purpose, functionality, and technical architecture. The strongest submissions solve a local or personal problem.
competitions.full_timeline: Registration opened June 2026. Final app submissions due late October 2026. Judged by your local congressional district office.
competitions.notes: Grades 6-12. District-based judging makes this the best odds-to-prestige ratio on the list.

competitions.name: CyberPatriot
competitions.cost_detail: $205 per team. Waived for Title I schools, all-female teams, JROTC, and Civil Air Patrol units.
competitions.why_it_helps: Hands-on network defense in a team, a distinctive cybersecurity credential few applicants have, with fee waivers for many teams.
competitions.what_it_is: The National Youth Cyber Defense Competition from the Air & Space Forces Association. Students act as IT professionals defending virtual networks.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: During 6-hour rounds, download virtual OS images, find hidden vulnerabilities, patch flaws, remove malware, and configure network defenses for points.
competitions.full_timeline: Registration opened May 2026, closes October 2026. Qualification rounds monthly October through December 2026. National finals spring 2027.
competitions.notes: BLOCKER: needs an adult coach and $205. Check the all-female team fee waiver, it removes the cost entirely.

competitions.name: picoCTF
competitions.why_it_helps: A Carnegie Mellon capture-the-flag cybersecurity contest you can do solo, no teacher, no cost, an easy and impressive entry into security.
competitions.what_it_is: A global online Capture The Flag cybersecurity competition built by security researchers at Carnegie Mellon.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Solve interactive challenges across web exploitation, cryptography, reverse engineering, binary exploitation, and digital forensics to find hidden flags and climb a live scoreboard.
competitions.full_timeline: Main competition runs online for two weeks in March 2027.
competitions.notes: Grades 6-12. Free and requires nobody's permission. Good entry point for anyone blocked out of CyberPatriot by the fee.

competitions.name: ASA Data Visualization Poster Competition
competitions.why_it_helps: Turn a data question into a visual poster, a low-barrier, solo-friendly way to show statistics and data skills.
competitions.what_it_is: A national statistics competition from the American Statistical Association focused on displaying data analysis visually.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Formulate a statistical research question, collect or source real data, analyze it, and design a digital poster with graphs, tables, and written explanation of your findings.
competitions.full_timeline: Digital poster submissions due April 1, 2027.
competitions.notes: High school categories split grades 7-9 and 10-12. If a student already has data from another project, this is nearly free to enter.

competitions.name: ASA Statistics Project Competition
competitions.why_it_helps: A complete statistical study from hypothesis to report, a rigorous, under-the-radar credential for data-minded students.
competitions.what_it_is: A national research competition from the American Statistical Association focused on formal statistical inquiry and scientific reporting.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Run a complete statistical study: define a hypothesis, collect raw data through surveys or experiments, analyze it with statistical methods, and write a formal report on process and conclusions.
competitions.full_timeline: Final written project reports due June 1, 2027.
competitions.notes: Grades 7-12. Latest deadline on the entire hub, which makes it the natural landing spot for a project that misses an earlier fair.

competitions.name: M3 Challenge
competitions.deadline_note: 14-hour weekend late Feb 2027; registration opens Nov 2026
competitions.why_it_helps: An intense 14-hour math modeling sprint on a real-world problem, a distinctive credential that shows applied math under pressure.
competitions.what_it_is: An internet-based math modeling contest from MathWorks and SIAM where teams solve real industrial or societal problems with math and data. Scholarship money for winners.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Pick a weekend inside the competition window, download the unseen problem prompt, and write a full mathematical model and research paper within 14 consecutive hours.
competitions.full_timeline: Registration opens November 2026. The 14-hour challenge weekend runs late February 2027.
competitions.notes: ELIGIBILITY: juniors and seniors only. Free, one weekend, real scholarship money. Best effort-to-reward ratio in this category.

competitions.name: HiMCM
competitions.why_it_helps: A two-week international math modeling contest, a substantial team research paper that shows sustained applied-math work.
competitions.what_it_is: An international mathematical modeling competition from COMAP for high school teams solving complex real-world problems.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Over a 14-day window, pick one of two real-world prompts, build mathematical models, test assumptions, and write a full research paper with your team.
competitions.full_timeline: Registration opens September 2026. The 14-day contest window runs early November 2026.
competitions.notes: Open to grades 9-12, unlike M3. Costs $100 where M3 is free, so run M3 unless a sophomore needs modeling experience.

competitions.name: We the People
competitions.cost_detail: Free at local and district levels. National finals participation involves school or chapter registration fees of $150 to $200 per team.
competitions.deadline_display: Regional and state competitions run November 2026 through February 2027
competitions.why_it_helps: Simulated congressional hearings on the Constitution, the gold-standard civics team competition for future law and policy students.
competitions.what_it_is: A national civic education program run as simulated congressional hearings, where high school teams demonstrate deep knowledge of the U.S. Constitution and Bill of Rights.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Work in student teams acting as constitutional expert witnesses. Prepare and present oral testimony, then answer spontaneous follow-up questions from a panel of judges in simulated congressional hearings.
competitions.full_timeline: Regional and state competitions November 2026 through February 2027. National Finals late April 2027.
competitions.notes: Requires a faculty coach, usually AP U.S. Government, AP U.S. History, or Civics, to register the school and oversee prep. Can run as a semester-long social studies elective or an after-school club. If your school has no chapter, you can ask an advisor to establish one.

competitions.name: JFK Profile in Courage Essay Contest
competitions.why_it_helps: A national essay run by the JFK Library, not a test-prep company, so few students know about it, a genuinely under-the-radar civics credential with real odds.
competitions.what_it_is: A national writing contest hosted by the John F. Kennedy Library Foundation honoring acts of political courage by elected officials.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Write a 700 to 1,000 word essay analyzing an act of political courage by a U.S. elected official who served during or after 1917. Detail the specific act, the obstacles and pressure the official faced, and the personal or political risks they accepted. The act can be at the local, state, national, or international level.
competitions.full_timeline: Submissions open September 1, 2026 and close January 11, 2027.

competitions.name: Voice of Democracy (VFW)
competitions.why_it_helps: A recorded audio essay on a patriotic theme submitted through a local VFW post, low barrier, solo, and community-rooted.
competitions.what_it_is: The Veterans of Foreign Wars audio-essay contest, in which high school students record their views on an annual patriotic theme.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Write and record a 3 to 5 minute audio essay on the annual patriotic theme, then submit the audio file with an entry form to your local VFW Post. Set up a free user profile, fill out the entry forms digitally, upload the files, and select your post so the local committee can judge it.
competitions.full_timeline: Submissions due October 31, 2026. Judged first by the local post, then district, state, and national rounds with scholarship money at each level.
competitions.notes: Mercer Island is VFW Post 5760 (vfwmercerisland.org). Do NOT say your name, school, city, or state anywhere in the written text or the audio recording. Judged first at a local post, so the first-round field is small.

competitions.name: American Legion Oratorical Contest
competitions.deadline_note: Applications open Nov 1, 2026; hard deadline Feb 1, 2027
competitions.deadline_display: Contact a local sponsor chapter by early January 2027
competitions.why_it_helps: A memorized constitutional speech contest, builds public-speaking and constitutional knowledge, strong for future lawyers and debaters.
competitions.what_it_is: A constitutional speech contest designed to build knowledge and appreciation of the U.S. Constitution among high school students.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Prepare and deliver an 8 to 10 minute memorized speech on an aspect of the U.S. Constitution, then deliver a 3 to 5 minute speech on a randomly drawn constitutional topic.
competitions.full_timeline: Applications open November 1, 2026 via waconstitutionalspeechcontest.org. Typical deadline to contact a local King County sponsor chapter and submit an initial speech draft or video is early January 2027. Hard application deadline February 1, 2027. Post and district rounds February through March 2027. State finals at Big Bend Community College, Moses Lake, WA, April 2-3, 2027. National Finals in Indianapolis, IN, April 22-24, 2027.
competitions.notes: Must be under age 20. Washington entries go through waconstitutionalspeechcontest.org. The early-January sponsor-chapter contact is the operative deadline. The February 1, 2027 application form date is a hard backstop, not the date to plan around.

competitions.name: Coolidge Scholarship
competitions.why_it_helps: A full-ride scholarship for academic merit and public-policy interest, elite and highly selective, juniors only.
competitions.what_it_is: A full-ride undergraduate scholarship from the Calvin Coolidge Presidential Foundation, awarded on academic merit, public policy interest, and commitment to public service.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Complete an extensive online application with several short and long essays on Calvin Coolidge, public policy, and leadership, plus letters of recommendation and transcripts.
competitions.full_timeline: Application portal opens late summer or early fall 2026 on the Coolidge Scholars Apply page. Final deadline expected around December 2026.
competitions.notes: ELIGIBILITY: grade 11 ONLY, juniors at the time of applying. Seniors are ineligible with no exceptions. Exact deadline not yet published, date shown is a projection. Recommendation letters take weeks to secure, so start in the fall.

competitions.name: Harvard International Review Essay Contest
competitions.why_it_helps: An analytical international-affairs essay for a Harvard publication, a recognizable name for policy-minded writers.
competitions.what_it_is: An academic writing competition hosted by the Harvard International Review encouraging analytical writing on international affairs.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Write an 800 to 1,200 word analytical, non-opinion article on one of the designated international affairs prompts, in AP Style. Top applicants advance to Defense Day.
competitions.full_timeline: Multiple cycles annually: Spring deadline in May, Summer deadline in August, Fall/Winter deadline January 2, 2027. Top applicants advance to Defense Day to present their argument to HIR judges.
competitions.notes: You must REGISTER separately to compete, submitting alone is not enough. Non-opinion means analytical, an op-ed will score badly.

competitions.name: LegalEagleBee Case and Defense Challenges
competitions.cost_detail: Costs range based on which event you enter. Check the site per event.
competitions.deadline_note: Case Comp Aug 30, 2026; Global Challenge stage 1 Oct 1
competitions.deadline_display: 9th Case Competition August 30, 2026, 12:00 to 1:00 PM PT
competitions.why_it_helps: An online exam on landmark Supreme Court cases, a fast, accessible first step for students exploring law.
competitions.what_it_is: An online legal knowledge and case analysis competition testing students on landmark Supreme Court cases, constitutional law, and judicial reasoning.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Study landmark Supreme Court precedents, then take an online exam on case facts, constitutional principles, and judicial opinions.
competitions.full_timeline: 9th Case Competition August 30, 2026, 12-1 PM PT. Legal Defense Global Challenge registration is open now and closes when the 500-team cap is reached. Stage 1 deadline October 1, 2026. Stage 2 deadline October 29, 2026.
competitions.notes: COST TIER BLANK: fee varies by event and is not stated as a single figure. The Global Challenge closes at a 500-team cap, not on a date, so it can close early. The Case Competition is a one-hour commitment.

competitions.name: Columbia Undergraduate Law Review Essay Contest
competitions.deadline_display: 2027 submission window expected to close June 26, 2027
competitions.why_it_helps: A legal analysis essay for a Columbia law publication, references real cases, a serious pre-law writing credential.
competitions.what_it_is: An annual writing contest from the Columbia Undergraduate Law Review inviting high schoolers to analyze legal, social, and constitutional issues.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Write a researched academic essay responding to the annual legal prompt in Chicago citation style. Your response must reference at least one court case or legal document.
competitions.full_timeline: 2027 competition is TBA. Submission window expected to end June 26, 2027. Monitor the official site.
competitions.notes: 2027 dates are TBA. The date shown is expected, not confirmed. Recheck before publishing.

competitions.name: Harvard Political Review Global Policy Case Competition
competitions.cost_detail: $45 to $85 registration fee per student, depending on submission deadline tier.
competitions.deadline_note: Priority deadline passed Aug 1, 2026; register ASAP
competitions.deadline_display: Priority deadline passed August 1, 2026. Later tiers still open.
competitions.why_it_helps: A policy opinion article for the Harvard Political Review, good for students who want to argue real political positions.
competitions.what_it_is: An international policy writing competition from the Harvard Political Review testing analytical and political writing.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Select a prompt on a pressing economic or global political issue and write an 800 to 1,200 word opinion article presenting an original policy argument in AP Style.
competitions.full_timeline: Priority deadline passed August 1, 2026. Later registration tiers remain open at higher fees. Final deadline not stated in source.
competitions.notes: DEADLINE BLANK: only the passed priority deadline is documented, no final date. Fee rises the later you register. Confirm the final deadline before publishing.

competitions.name: Bill of Rights Institute MyImpact Challenge
competitions.why_it_helps: Run a community project and connect it to founding principles, pairs real service with civics writing, an under-the-radar credential with a long runway.
competitions.what_it_is: A service-learning competition where you run a local volunteer or civic project and connect it in writing to American founding principles and civic virtues.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Write an essay of up to 1,200 words connecting your community project to at least one Founding Principle and one Civic Virtue from the BRI framework, plus a 2,000 word project report breaking down what you actually did.
competitions.full_timeline: Submissions open September 2026, deadline May 3, 2027. Fall: pick your community topic, design the project, and choose a Civic Virtue and Founding Principle. Winter: run the project and document it with photos and video. Spring: write the essay and project report and submit.
competitions.notes: START BY SEPTEMBER 1, 2026. This is a year-long commitment disguised as an essay contest: the community project has to actually run in fall and winter before you can write about it in spring. A student who finds this in April has already missed it. Open to grades 8 to 12, ages 13 to 19.

competitions.name: Constituting America “We the Future” Contest
competitions.why_it_helps: Express constitutional principles through essay, film, song, or STEM, creative and flexible, an easy on-ramp to civics.
competitions.what_it_is: A creative civic competition inspiring students to study the U.S. Constitution and founding documents through academic and artistic mediums. Awards scholarships up to $5,000, national exposure, and a paid winner mentorship trip.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Create and submit an original project based on your grade category prompt. Depending on age group this can be a written essay, a song, a short film, a PSA, a social media video, or a tech or STEM project.
competitions.full_timeline: Submission window is open now and closes May 31, 2027.
competitions.notes: Ages 14-19. Entries must be completely free of AI assistance. Team of 2 applies to the STEM category only. If under 18, a parent, guardian, or teacher must assist with the upload.

competitions.name: Princeton Legal Journal High School Essay Contest
competitions.why_it_helps: A rigorous constitutional-law essay with winners published by Princeton's legal journal, a top-tier pre-law credential.
competitions.what_it_is: An annual legal writing competition run by the undergraduate editorial board of the Princeton Legal Journal, with publication for the top three authors.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Research and draft an analytical essay between 1,500 and 3,000 words excluding footnotes, answering the annual constitutional legal theme. Proper legal academic citations are mandatory.
competitions.full_timeline: New prompt drops early spring 2027. Submission deadline expected mid-May 2027. Top three authors go through a collaborative editing process with the board and are published in the journal.
competitions.notes: Date is expected mid-May, not confirmed. Submissions are reviewed anonymously, so identifying information in the essay body or file metadata can disqualify you.

competitions.name: United States Senate Youth Program (USSYP)
competitions.deadline_display: Washington State deadline September 25, 2026, 4:00 PM PT
competitions.why_it_helps: Two delegates per state attend a week in DC with a $12,500 scholarship, elite and highly selective, requires an elected leadership position.
competitions.what_it_is: A highly selective national program funded by The Hearst Foundations that selects two student delegates per state for an intensive public service week in Washington D.C. Delegates receive a $12,500 undergraduate scholarship.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Apply through your state education department portal. The bundle requires an activities resume, transcripts, letters of recommendation from school administrators, and a response to the Washington state 2026-27 essay prompt. If selected you must attend the full Washington Week program to receive the scholarship.
competitions.full_timeline: WA state deadline September 25, 2026 at 4:00 PM PT. Other state windows close through September and October 2026. Selected delegates must attend Washington Week, March 6-13, 2027.
competitions.notes: ELIGIBILITY: must currently hold a high-level elected or appointed leadership position such as Student Body or Class President, VP, Secretary, Treasurer, or Student Council Rep. The student applies individually, but the application requires recommendation letters from school administrators, which take weeks to obtain. Request them first.

competitions.name: Bennington Young Writers Awards
competitions.why_it_helps: A national poetry/fiction/nonfiction contest from Bennington, a low-barrier, recognizable creative-writing credential.
competitions.what_it_is: A national creative writing competition hosted by Bennington College recognizing original fiction, nonfiction, and poetry.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Submit original work under 1,500 words in one of three categories: Poetry (a collection of 1 to 3 poems), Fiction (a short story or standalone excerpt), or Nonfiction (a personal or academic essay).
competitions.full_timeline: Submissions open September 1, 2026 and close November 1, 2026.
competitions.notes: Requires sponsor teacher approval even though the student submits directly. Ask the teacher before the last week of October.

competitions.name: Scholastic Art & Writing Awards
competitions.cost_detail: $10 per individual entry, $30 per portfolio. Fee waivers available inside the platform.
competitions.deadline_note: Dec 1, 2026 for Region-at-Large West; up to Jan 6
competitions.why_it_helps: The most prestigious creative program for students across 28 categories, a National Medal is a nationally recognized honor.
competitions.what_it_is: The nation's longest-running and most prestigious creative recognition program for middle and high school students, spanning 28 categories of art and writing.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Submit original artwork or writing through the online system to your regional affiliate. Categories include short stories, critical essays, poetry, journalism, and visual art portfolios.
competitions.full_timeline: December 1, 2026 for early regions including Region-at-Large West. Later regions run to January 6, 2027. Regional judging feeds national recognition.
competitions.notes: King County students register under the Region-at-Large West affiliate, deadline December 1. Confirm your affiliate by school location, the national date is not your date. Account setup requires parent or guardian and educator approval, so start before Thanksgiving.

competitions.name: The Concord Review
competitions.deadline_note: Rolling quarterly: Nov 1, Feb 1, May 1, Aug 1
competitions.why_it_helps: The only journal publishing high-school history research, being published is an elite, rare humanities credential.
competitions.what_it_is: The only quarterly peer-reviewed academic journal in the world that publishes independent history research papers written by secondary school students.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Write and submit an original, deeply researched history paper between 5,000 and 15,000 words with comprehensive Turabian or Chicago-style endnotes.
competitions.full_timeline: Fixed quarterly submission dates: November 1, February 1, May 1, and August 1. Next is November 1, 2026.
competitions.notes: 5,000 words minimum is a semester of work, not an essay. The quarterly cycle means missing November costs you three months, not a year. Highest word count and highest fee in this category.

competitions.name: New York Times Student Contests
competitions.deadline_note: Tiny Memoir Sep 16-Oct 28, 2026; ~6 more through the year
competitions.why_it_helps: Short, frequent writing challenges from the NYT Learning Network, the 100-word Tiny Memoir is the single easiest entry point on the whole site.
competitions.what_it_is: A year-long series of writing, commentary, and multimedia challenges from The New York Times Learning Network.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Produce and submit work answering the seasonal contest prompt, using NYT articles or original self-expression depending on the contest.
competitions.full_timeline: My Tiny Memoir, a 100-word narrative, runs September 16 to October 28, 2026. Roughly six more contests run across the rest of the year, each with its own window.
competitions.notes: Ages 13-19. Seven or so separate contests per year, each with its own deadline and format. The date shown is the next one, not the only one. A 100-word memoir is the cheapest entry on this entire hub.

competitions.name: National History Day
competitions.cost_detail: Free to $15, varies by region and district.
competitions.deadline_note: School contests Jan-early Feb 2027; state late Apr
competitions.why_it_helps: Primary-source history research in five formats (documentary, exhibit, paper, performance, website), flexible and well-recognized.
competitions.what_it_is: An annual project-based historical research competition built around primary-source research on a yearly theme.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Conduct original historical research and present it in one of five formats: Documentary, Exhibit, Paper, Performance, or Website. Compete through local, regional, and state levels to reach Nationals.
competitions.full_timeline: School-level contests January to early February 2027 if more than one team competes. Regional registration mid-February 2027. Washington State History Day Finals late April to early May 2027. National Finals at the University of Maryland, College Park, June 13-17, 2027.
competitions.notes: BLOCKER: requires a sponsoring teacher to register the school. Senior Division is grades 9-12. Research must start in the fall to be ready for a January school contest.

competitions.name: Adroit Prizes for Poetry and Prose
competitions.why_it_helps: Highly selective international creative-writing prizes, recognition here signals real literary talent.
competitions.what_it_is: Highly selective international creative writing prizes awarded annually by the editors of The Adroit Journal.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Submit up to six poems for the Poetry Prize, or up to three stories or essays totaling under 3,500 words for the Prose Prize.
competitions.full_timeline: Submissions open April 1 and close May 1, 2027. One-month window.
competitions.notes: Open to high schoolers and undergraduates, so you are competing against college students. One-month window with no early submission.

competitions.name: Princeton Ten-Minute Play Contest
competitions.deadline_note: Portal opens Jan 2027; strict 250-submission cap (juniors only)
competitions.deadline_display: Portal launches January 2027, closes at 250 submissions
competitions.why_it_helps: A Princeton playwriting contest for juniors only, a distinctive creative credential with a hard submission cap, so enter early.
competitions.what_it_is: A national playwriting competition organized by the Lewis Center for the Arts at Princeton University.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Write and submit an original short play up to 10 pages in standard theatrical script format.
competitions.full_timeline: Digital submission portal launches January 2027. A strict quota of 250 submissions shuts the portal for the year, so it can close early.
competitions.notes: ELIGIBILITY: grade 11 ONLY. CLOSES AT A CAP, NOT A DATE: 250 submissions ends it. Have the script finished before January or the portal may be gone. Date shown is an estimate of the opening, not a published deadline.

competitions.name: Bow Seat Ocean Awareness Contest
competitions.why_it_helps: Creative work on ocean and environmental themes across many mediums, open-ended and beginner-friendly.
competitions.what_it_is: An international creative arts competition encouraging young people to advocate for ocean health and environmental conservation.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Submit original work in Visual Art, Creative Writing, Film, Interactive and Multimedia, Performing Arts, or Poetry and Spoken Word addressing the annual environmental theme.
competitions.full_timeline: Submissions open September 2026 and close June 8, 2027.
competitions.notes: Senior division is ages 15-18, Junior division ages 11-14. Cross-tags to STEM and environment, so it also fits a science-minded student.

competitions.name: YoungArts National Writing Competition
competitions.why_it_helps: The premier national talent search for young writers, YoungArts recognition is a serious, career-signaling honor.
competitions.what_it_is: The premier national recognition program and talent search for high school writers, hosted by the National YoungArts Foundation.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Submit a creative writing portfolio through the YoungArts portal in Creative Nonfiction, Fiction, Novel, Play or Screenplay, Poetry, or Spoken Word.
competitions.full_timeline: Submission portal is open now with a deadline of October 6, 2026 at 5:00 PM PT.
competitions.notes: Ages 15-18. A portfolio, not a single piece, so pieces need to already exist. Fee waivers are available in the platform.

competitions.name: Ayn Rand Institute Essay Contests
competitions.deadline_note: Atlas Shrugged Nov 6, 2026; Anthem & Fountainhead Apr 30, 2027
competitions.why_it_helps: Read a novel and write an analytical essay to set prompts, a straightforward, free, solo way to show critical reading.
competitions.what_it_is: A long-standing series of literary essay competitions evaluating critical thinking on the philosophical concepts in Ayn Rand's novels.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Read the designated novel and submit an analytical, text-supported essay answering strict pre-published prompts.
competitions.full_timeline: Staggered deadlines by book. Atlas Shrugged closes November 6, 2026. Anthem closes April 30, 2027. The Fountainhead closes April 30, 2027.
competitions.notes: GRADE VARIES BY BOOK: Anthem is grades 8-10, The Fountainhead is grades 11-12, Atlas Shrugged is grade 12 plus undergraduate and graduate. The soonest deadline shown is Atlas Shrugged, which seniors only are eligible for.

competitions.name: AFSA National High School Essay Contest
competitions.why_it_helps: A diplomacy and foreign-service essay, a strong fit for students interested in international relations (note: eligibility restrictions apply).
competitions.what_it_is: A civics and diplomacy essay contest run by the American Foreign Service Association to engage students in the role of international relations.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Write a 1,000 to 1,500 word analytical essay on the annual prompt, identifying how the U.S. Foreign Service resolved an international crisis or peace-building mission.
competitions.full_timeline: Portal opens in early fall when the prompt is announced, usually September or October 2026. Closes March 1, 2027 at 8:59 PM PST.
competitions.notes: ELIGIBILITY: strictly limited to children of U.S. citizens who are NOT members of the Foreign Service. Check this before writing.

competitions.name: Patricia Grodd Poetry Prize
competitions.deadline_display: Portal open November 1 to November 30 only
competitions.why_it_helps: Submit one poem to The Kenyon Review, winners get early recognition from a top literary magazine, sophomores and juniors only.
competitions.what_it_is: An internationally respected youth poetry award from the editors of The Kenyon Review, one of the most selective literary magazines in the country.
competitions.what_you_need_to_do: Submit one single original unpublished poem, any length, any style.
competitions.full_timeline: The application portal is open strictly from November 1 through November 30. No submissions outside that window.
competitions.notes: ELIGIBILITY: grades 10 and 11 ONLY. Seniors and freshmen are ineligible. One poem, free, thirty-day window. Lowest effort entry in this category.
